doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: An Elvin quartet gig in 1971 and Joe Farrell's flute playing
summary: Kirchner recalls first hearing the band at a Goddard Riverside concert; both praise Joe Farrell's flute and Liebman explains why he stopped playing it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I heard one of those gigs. The first time I ever heard you, I was just 18. I had just come to New York to go to college. This is the fall of ’71. There was an ad in the Voice for this little gig. It was a free concert with Elvin’s quartet at this place on the Upper West Side called the Goddard Riverside Community Center, in the 90s on Amsterdam. It’s still there. I went there, and there was – it was this little auditorium, no sound system. They just set up on the floor. It was you, Joe Farrell, Gene, and Elvin. It was – I can still remember it vividly. I can remember Three Card Monte, For All the Other Times.
That’s it. That’s the book.
I remember Joe playing this . . .
Fancy Free.
You didn’t play that.
No, because that’s with Grossman. That’s right.
Joe played this outrageous flute solo on . . .
Time for Love.
No, it was . . .
My Ship.
. . . My Ship. I think . . .
That was his thing.
Is it just me? I think Joe Farrell is the unsung great flute player in jazz of all
Thank you. Thank you very much. I totally agree with you.
I don’t think anybody in jazz has ever played the flute like Joe.
Lew [Tabackin] is . . .
And Hubert [Laws].
Hubert, but real jazz. Nothing personal.
Neither of them have the command of harmony.
Hubert is the flute player of all time, but as far as jazz goes, Lew – Lew great, but Joe for the depth of ideas.
He took all of Coltrane’s shit, harmonically, and brought it into flute . . .
I totally agree with that.
. . . in a way that nobody else has ever done.

I loved – I also felt – I didn’t – I didn’t say I didn’t like it, but on tenor and soprano, he was good. He was very good. But on flute, he was exemplary, no question. I totally agree with you. Then I had to play flute after him. Can you imagine me getting up and playing Time for Love or My Ship, after hearing him do it? This was – but Elvin said, “You’re going to play flute.”
You’re a better – as jazz guys go, you’re a better than average flute player.
Yeah, but I stopped it because of that. I didn’t want to be second best. That instrument, you’ve got to hit that every day. This is not – you don’t just take – saxophone you can . . .
Joe was a flute major in college.

As was Lew, as is Hubert. That makes a difference. That’s why you – that’s great. I don’t remember that gig. But this was – Joe didn’t say a word to me. I don’t know if Joe was just the way he was. I don’t know anything about him.
